202B.10 / CHAPTER 10 OF 11

Comprehensive swing check

What brings the next buyers, can the token survive, and is ownership strengthening?

11 chapters with worked investigations

01Price structure02Base & repricing03Supply zones04Demand & absorption05Holder rotation06Expansion & pullback07Continuation vs distribution08Swing lifecycle09Retracement references: 0.5 & 0.61810Comprehensive swing check11How to trade the swing

01Definition

For a 3-14 day swing, deepen the same three basic entry checks from 202A.10: thesis, quality and upside; survival and dump risk; participants and demand conversion. The longer exposure needs a more comprehensive assessment before entry.

02Why it matters

A swing needs enough survival time for the expected demand wave to develop, and enough remaining upside to justify exposure. A stable chart, respected dev, or large KOL audience alone does not establish either.

03What to check

  • Thesis, quality and upside — what can create the next demand wave?
    • Dev reputation and delivery: Check relevant history and current delivery. Where there is a product, distinguish its existence from actual use; a pure meme can depend on culture and creators instead.
    • KOL outreach and community: Assess KOL quality, reach across different audiences and persistence, plus organic community activity. Who can keep attracting tomorrow’s buyers?
    • Meta, catalysts and upside: Identify catalysts within 3-14 days, renewable attention, distribution and any economics linking success to token demand. Compare current MC/FDV with credible peers and explain differences.
  • Survival and dump risk — can the token last until that demand arrives?
    • Contract and liquidity: Verify exact-CA legitimacy, contract controls, liquidity control and an executable exit for the intended size.
    • Dev behavior and linked supply: Check holdings and actual sales, bundles, linked wallets and discretionary concentration. Reputation does not clear current selling risk.
    • Early supply overhang: Identify cheap inventory and remaining sellable supply. Could current or expected demand absorb it within the holding window?
  • Participants and demand conversion — who owns it, and is demand broadening?
    • Who is positioned: Identify meaningful holders, KOLs and related wallets; compare actual accumulation, holding and distribution over time.
    • Attention conversion: Check whether new attention brings fresh buyers, holder growth and repeat participation; do not substitute mentions or follower counts for conversion.
    • Demand versus sellers: Check buy/sell flow, volume quality and absorption. Is independent demand broadening enough to meet existing supply?

04Healthy / Dangerous

Healthy

A credible narrative, creator or product demand engine can renew attention inside the swing window. Independent attention converts into buyers, and ownership and liquidity can withstand selling. The largest dependency and unknowns are explicit.

Dangerous

Reputation substitutes for checking dev sales, follower counts substitute for demand, or cheap insider inventory can overwhelm incoming buyers. A distant roadmap or recycled promotion is the only reason offered for a run.

05Beginner mistake

Calling quiet price action accumulation, treating all KOL posts as independent outreach, or assuming a good project automatically gives its token upside.

06Takeaway

Conclude with why it can run, what can kill it, and its largest dependency. Keep evidence brief and mark unknowns explicitly; passing the check does not automatically justify entry.

The same three entry checks, with greater depth for a 3-14 day swing.

SURVIVE → ATTRACT → CONVERT → REPRICE.

Why it can run / what can kill it / largest dependency.

ILLUSTRATIVE · NOT A LIVE TOKEN

See the idea

  1. 01

    Thesis / quality / upside: an active cultural meme has new creator content and KOLs reaching distinct audiences over the next week. There is no product release. Compare current valuation with credible peers and identify why more people could buy.

  2. 02

    Survival / dump risk: the exact CA and links agree, but linked early wallets retain cheap inventory. Verify contract controls, actual sales and exit quotes; credible promoters do not clear this overhang.

  3. 03

    Participants / conversion: new independent buyers and holders increase after content reaches those audiences. Check whether they absorb early selling. The largest dependency is continued outside attention, not merely existing holders repeating the story.

WORKED INVESTIGATION · ILLUSTRATIVE

Work through the evidence

Mechanism and worked case

Illustrative narrative swing: a cultural meme has no product, but creators publish fresh content and KOLs repeatedly reach different audiences. Independent buyer and holder counts increase over comparable windows. Linked early wallets still retain cheap inventory, so survival risk needs checking against selling and usable liquidity. The thesis depends on continued external attention. A separate product-led setup could depend on a day-seven release; both must convert attention into token demand.

How to investigate it

Record three short evidence summaries with sources and check times. For thesis and upside, verify delivery, KOL quality/reach/persistence, catalyst dates, comparables and the link to token demand. For survival, inspect contract control, liquidity, dev sales, linked supply and early cost bases where history allows. For participants, compare holdings and actual sales over consistent windows with fresh buyers, holder growth and absorption. Mark gaps Unknown and finish with why it can run, what can kill it, and its largest dependency.

Check your reasoning — answered

A respected dev ships on time and KOL mentions triple, but a linked group sells into every buying burst and price makes little progress. Is the swing cleared? No. Reputation and attention do not resolve survival risk or establish conversion into sustained demand. Investigate whether fresh buyers can absorb that supply before shaping the trade.

Try it on a token

See it in Meme Fast → Swing

Use fresh listing context, source evidence, and sampled flow in Inspect as leads. Verify dev history, KOL outreach, bundles, permissions, holder behavior and catalysts externally. RSS counts and wallet snapshots are incomplete evidence.

Go deeper

Separate dev reputation from current behavior: past delivery supports credibility, while current holdings, sales and contract control determine risk. Separate product existence from evidence of real usage. For KOL outreach, distinguish quality, reach across non-overlapping audiences, and persistence beyond a single paid or promotional post. For upside, look for external validation, ecosystem proof, an independent attention source, or a recurring catalyst engine; product or child-asset success needs a believable link to token demand. Compare market cap and FDV with adoption and credible peers rather than mechanically copying their valuations. Check volume quality, unique participation and holder growth over comparable windows; wash activity and coordinated wallets can distort them. Quiet-price discussion matters only if fresh participation can renew. Confirmed sell traps, dangerous contract control, removable liquidity or overwhelming insider distribution can invalidate the setup regardless of narrative strength. Unknown critical safety or execution information leaves the entry unresolved. No numerical total is required.
